patches.reason: m = qBr/v = (1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹)(0.50)(0.20)/(2.0 × 10⁶) = 1.6 × 10⁻²⁰/2.0 × 10⁶ = 8.0 × 10⁻²⁷ kg, which is choice A. The published explanation gets 8.0 × 10⁻²⁷ right the first time, then a "Wait, recalculating" step reports the same product as 1.6 × 10⁻²⁶ — off by a factor of two — and the key followed the mistaken line.

patches.old: For circular motion in a magnetic field, qvB = mv^2/r, so m = qBr/v. Substituting q = 1.6 x 10^-19 C, B = 0.50 T, r = 0.20 m, and v = 2.0 x 10^6 m/s gives m = (1.6 x 10^-19)(0.50)(0.20)/(2.0 x 10^6) = 8.0 x 10^-27 kg. Wait, recalculating: (1.6e-19 x 0.50 x 0.20) / (2.0e6) = 1.6e-26 kg. Choice A is a common error from misplacing a factor of 2.
patches.new: Set the magnetic force equal to the centripetal force: qvB = mv^2/r, which gives r = mv/(qB) and therefore m = qBr/v. Substituting q = 1.6 x 10^-19 C, B = 0.50 T, r = 0.20 m and v = 2.0 x 10^6 m/s: the numerator is (1.6 x 10^-19)(0.50)(0.20) = 1.6 x 10^-20, and dividing by 2.0 x 10^6 gives m = 8.0 x 10^-27 kg. Work the powers of ten separately from the digits to avoid the usual slip here; choice B is exactly twice the right answer, and choice C is five times it.
patches.reason: Rewritten: the published version contained the arithmetic error that produced the wrong key, and its closing sentence described choice A — the correct answer — as the common error.

patches.old: The radius in the magnetic field is r = mv/qB = sqrt(2mV/q)/B x sqrt(m).
patches.new: The radius in the magnetic field is r = mv/(qB); substituting v = sqrt(2qV/m) gives r = sqrt(2mV/q)/B.
patches.reason: The published formula is garbled: it sets r equal to sqrt(2mV/q)/B and then multiplies by an extra sqrt(m), which is dimensionally wrong. The substitution gives r = sqrt(2mV/q)/B on its own, and that expression already shows the r ∝ sqrt(m) dependence the next sentence relies on.

visual.title: Right hand, circle, and what the force cannot do
visual.alt: The right-hand rule with fingers along v, curling to B and the thumb giving the force on a positive charge, reversed for a negative one; a charge entering a field into the page and circling with radius mv over qB and a period that does not depend on its speed; a table contrasting the electric force, which acts on any charge, points along E and does work, with the magnetic force, which acts only on moving charges, points perpendicular to v and B and does none; parallel wires attracting with like currents and repelling with opposed ones; and a mass spectrometer in which the heavier isotope sweeps the wider arc.
visual.caption: Everything here follows from the force being perpendicular to the velocity: it can bend the path into a circle, but it can never add a joule of kinetic energy.
